climateNote: This is a volcanic-system event: magma inflow and dike intrusion drive the motion, not any climate-linked process. Fringe shows it for radar physics and hazard-monitoring value — no climate connection is claimed.

dataset.mission: Sentinel-1A/1B (Copernicus), 12-day repeat; COSMO-SkyMed spot acquisitions in published studies
dataset.datasetId: Icelandic Met Office deformation series (GNSS + InSAR); Copernicus Sentinel-1 SLC
dataset.window: Published: Oct 2023 – Jan 2026 inflation–eruption cycles; in-app pass-pair window: 120 days
dataset.coverage: Reykjanes Peninsula — Svartsengi / Sundhnúkur crater row (~40 km scene)
dataset.gnss: REYK, Nevada Geodetic Lab daily IGS20 solutions, bundled as weekly means — quiet far-field reference 40 km NE of the dome
dataset.processing: Published: joint GNSS + InSAR pressure-source inversion (Parks et al., 2025). In-app: elastic Mogi point source at 4.5 km depth; one fringe = λ/2 line-of-sight motion

items.label: MEASURED
items.detail: Real daily IGS20 solutions from NGL station REYK (far-field reference), downsampled to weekly means, bundled and charted in-app.

items.label: MEASURED
items.detail: 3–4 mm/day onset uplift (Þorbjörn, Jan 2020, Icelandic Met Office); 4–5 km pressure-source depth (Parks et al., 2025); 9 eruptions Dec 2023–Jan 2026. Shown as citations; not re-derived in-app.

items.label: MODELED
items.detail: Physics rendering of an elastic Mogi source (0.02 km³ at 4.5 km depth) tuned to the published geometry. NOT a raw SAR image — computed on-device.

items.label: DERIVED
items.detail: Computed on-device from the physical model (one fringe = λ/2 LOS). Tracks the model, not a downloaded product.

items.label: LIVE
items.detail: Live accelerometer from the demo ESP32 ground station — IoT demo at the demo site; not a satellite measurement of this event.

limitations: The interferogram is a physics rendering of published figures, not raw SAR pixels — no SAR processing is done in-app.
Mogi source parameters are simplified; the real system involves multiple sills and dikes.
Far-field reference station REYK does not capture near-dome deformation.
